item.title: Databricks Introduces Agentic Identity Resolution for Customer Data Platforms
item.description:
Databricks Introduces Agentic Identity Resolution for Customer Data Platforms

📚 Introduction

Databricks has launched Agentic Identity Resolution, an approach that combines deterministic, probabilistic, and LLM-based matching to connect fragmented customer records. This capability is part of CustomerLake, designed to help data teams build trusted datasets and enable marketers to activate audiences faster.

🧩 How It Works

The process involves several steps:

  • Run deterministic rules first (exact email, exact phone, a partner ID that maps to your customer ID), then score the gaps with probabilistic matching.
  • Cluster the matches and mint, or keep, a persistent ID.
  • Build layers using Spark Declarative Pipelines and run identity resolution after silver, with the canonical ID becoming the join key for gold.

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Description
Agentic Identity Resolution Combines deterministic, probabilistic, and LLM-based matching to connect fragmented records
Profile Agents Handle heavy lifting of matching and golden-record survivorship
Manual data steward overrides Allow teams to apply human judgment where needed

Agentic CDP requires:

  • The right sources, clean data, one identity per customer, and golden profiles marketers trust.
  • Agents handle matching records and drafting audiences while people choose sources, review matches, and approve actions.
  • Identity resolution runs next to data, making ownership of the identity graph practical.

📏 Data Model Approach

  • Part 1 of a two-part series focusing on modeling from raw data to omnichannel activation.
  • Part 2 covers mapping B2C and B2B datasets, attributes, and use cases onto the model.
  • Identity is matched nightly inside a tool, owned, explainable and reversible, with an audit-able identity graph using a persistent ID.

🚀 Availability

  • Can be built with SQL rules plus open-source matchers like Splink or Zingg.
  • Or use CustomerLake, where Profile Agents handle the heavy lifting.
  • Data teams can define trusted datasets once through Databricks and Unity Catalog.

💡 Why It Matters

Brands long asked why they couldn’t own their identity graph and run deterministic matching on their own data. With identity resolution running next to the data, owning the graph becomes practical, and in our experience it’s the most important table you’ll build.

#AIagents #CDP #CustomerData #IdentityResolution #Databricks

Source: Data Modeling Best Practices for an Agentic CDP, Part 1: The Data Foundation

item.title: Databricks introduces Tag Exchange to share Unity Catalog tags via Iceberg
item.description:
Databricks introduces Tag Exchange to share Unity Catalog tags via Iceberg

Databricks announced support for catalog labels, a new capability in the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API that enables platforms, engines, and agents to access context such as business purpose, ownership, and data classifications maintained in Iceberg REST-compatible catalogs. This development addresses the issue of metadata context remaining siloed in source catalogs, which previously forced teams to recreate classifications across platforms or maintain custom metadata synchronization pipelines.

🧩 How it works

Databricks worked with the Apache Iceberg community to add an optional labels field to the Iceberg REST LoadTable response. This provides a standard way for catalogs to expose table- and column-level context to other platforms, tools, and agents.

  • Labels format: String key-value pairs that describe business ownership, intended use, sensitivity, or other catalog-maintained context.
  • Flexibility: The standard defines a common format for sharing metadata without prescribing vocabulary or interpretation, allowing each platform to build on it in its own way.
  • Example: A table named support_cases can carry labels like domain=customer_support or system.certification_status=certified. An authorized data steward can also assign column-level labels, such as content_type=support_case_summary for an issue_summary column.

⚙️ Key details

Tag Exchange is Databricks’ implementation of this standard, exposing Unity Catalog’s table- and column-level tags through the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API. This makes catalog metadata available directly to Python applications, including data-discovery tools and agents.

  • Open Governance: Context maintained in one system becomes usable across every platform, engine, and AI agent working with the data.
  • Reusability: Enterprises can reuse classifications and business context for discovery, agent workflows, and access policies.
  • Interoperability: Each tool retains the freedom to decide how to interpret and use that context, while the catalog’s metadata remains intact across platforms.

Databricks is joined by Google Cloud, Salesforce, ClickHouse, Atlan, Collibra, DataHub, Immuta, Trust3 AI, PhoenixAI, and Datastrato in advancing this shared vision of metadata interoperability.

🚀 Availability

Tag Exchange is available in Beta today. To get started, users can enable “Tag Exchange via Iceberg REST Catalog” in the Databricks Previews portal.

💡 Why it matters

This capability allows sensitivity labels set once in Unity Catalog to drive policy in external platforms without separate metadata projects. As noted by Don Bosco Durai, CTO of Trust3 AI, a sensitivity label set once in Unity Catalog can now drive policy in platforms like Trust3 AI without a separate metadata project. Similarly, Chandru Sugunan, Director of Product at Atlan, noted that open metadata exchange through the Iceberg REST Catalog lets enterprises keep context intact across every platform they choose to run.

#Databricks #ApacheIceberg #Metadata #TagExchange #DataGovernance #Interoperability

Source: Sharing catalog metadata across data platforms, engines, and agents

item.title: Databricks Launches Native Lakebase Sink for Apache Spark Structured Streaming
item.description:
Databricks Launches Native Lakebase Sink for Apache Spark Structured Streaming

Databricks has announced the general availability of a native Lakebase sink for Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming, simplifying real-time data ingestion into its serverless PostgreSQL offering. The connector eliminates the need for custom foreach writers, reducing complexity in building low-latency feature pipelines for use cases like fraud detection and recommendation systems.

📣 What Happened

Today, Databricks is releasing the native Lakebase sink for Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming. This connector writes computed results directly to Lakebase and handles batching, retries, and upserts automatically, removing the burden of building and maintaining custom infrastructure.

🔍 Why It Matters

Low-latency use cases such as fraud detection, live personalization, and real-time feature computation require results in a serving-ready OLTP store. Lakebase Postgres is a fully managed, serverless PostgreSQL database with autoscaling, branching, native Unity Catalog integration, and sub-10ms reads. Previously, writing to Lakebase from a streaming pipeline required developers to build custom foreach writers to manage batching, retries, and upserts — a complex task that was difficult to scale and maintain.

The new native sink handles these concerns internally. You can wire up a Lakebase write in minutes with a single writeStream call, without needing to manage performance, tuning, or maintenance.

⚙️ Key Features

  • Fully managed, serverless PostgreSQL database with autoscaling and native Unity Catalog integration
  • Sub-10ms read latency
  • Native Lakebase sink for Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming
  • Supports both micro-batch and Real-Time Mode
  • Automatic upsert handling with upsertKey — maintains one row per key
  • Built-in connection pooling, batching, and retries
  • Seamless credentials management via running user or service principal
  • Table creation if it does not exist
  • Real-time data ingestion using .toTable() for Unity Catalog-registered tables
  • Direct write using format("postgresql") for non-Unity Catalog tables or external PostgreSQL databases

🧩 Use Case Example: Real-Time Recommendation Features

A video streaming platform wants to recommend videos by leveraging users’ recent activity. The pipeline ingests WATCH and LIKE events from Kafka, computes the last 6 videos watched and the last 3 liked per user, and upserts one feature row per user into Lakebase in hundreds of milliseconds. At inference time, a recommendation model looks up each user’s feature row by user_id to rank what to show next.

The pipeline uses transformWithState to maintain per-user state and emit one feature row per user, with writing to Lakebase handled by a single writeStream and .toTable() call.

🚀 Availability and Benchmarks

The native sink is now generally available. In testing, the pipeline processed ~20K events per second against 5 million active users using a 40-core classic compute (DBR 18 LTS) writing to an 8-CU Lakebase project with 5-minute RTM checkpoint intervals. End-to-end latency from Kafka input timestamp to row landing in Lakebase was 100–200 milliseconds, with query latency in single digits via Lakebase.

💬 Customer Feedback

  • “We stream real-time data into Lakebase so our risk agent can pull a user’s recent activity when it investigates an alert. We initially built that path with a custom ForeachWriter, which meant building and maintaining the write infrastructure ourselves. As part of our development work, we found that the native sink reduces the custom work required for connection pooling, batching, and retries.” — Maria Marinova, Sr. Lead Software Engineer, DraftKings
  • “Testing real-time data flows into Lakebase is an important part of validating how our risk agent can quickly access the freshest available user data when making decisions. As we evaluated the native sink, we found that its built-in connection pooling, batching, and retries reduce the custom infrastructure we need to build and maintain.” — Georgi Stoychev, Sr. Software Automation Engineer, DraftKings

📊 Technical Details

Feature Description
Upsert Key Sink maintains one row per key
Connection Pooling Built-in, managed automatically
Batching Automatically handled for throughput
Retries Transient failure handling with backoff
Credentials Managed as running user or service principal
Table Creation Automatically created if not present
Latency End-to-end 100–200ms; query latency single-digit milliseconds

🔗 Getting Started

For a deeper look at the implementation, see the companion repo — a self-serve example you can run end-to-end.

Image: https://www.databricks.com/sites/default/files/2023-08/databricks-default.png?v=1712162038

#Databricks #Lakebase #ApacheSpark #Real-TimeStreaming #FeatureEngineering

Source: Announcing General Availability of native Lakebase Postgres sink for Spark Structured Streaming

item.title: Databricks Genie One Combines Curated Agents and Governed Layer for 93-95% Accuracy
item.description:
Databricks Genie One Combines Curated Agents and Governed Layer for 93-95% Accuracy

Databricks has released Genie One, powered by the generally available Genie Ontology, which integrates business context into analytics by combining curated agents with a governed semantic layer to resolve contradictory metrics across teams.

🔍 Overview

  • Genie One uses Genie Ontology to bring business context into the analytics experience.
  • Genie Ontology learns from existing team work (dashboards, queries, notebooks, semantic models) as Ontology Snippets.
  • This learned knowledge is complemented by a governed layer: explicitly defined business concepts in Unity Catalog via certified Metric Views, Domains and Subdomains, and Pages.
  • A study compared four Genie Agents (Finance, Reserving, Underwriting, Claims) using the same tables but team-specific definitions, queries, and documents.
  • The study also tested a fictional retailer to validate findings outside insurance.

🧩 How it works

  • Genie One does not simply select one agent for every question.
  • It can use governed Unity Catalog Semantics (Metric Views, Domains and subdomains, Pages) or route a question to a relevant Genie Agent.
  • If no suitable match is found, it searches the workspace.
  • When answering using its own context, Genie One does not automatically inherit the instructions configured inside each agent.

⚙️ Key details

Agent setup

  • Four agents shared the same underlying tables.
  • Each agent had access to its team’s folder of documents (14 PDFs total across four folders).
  • Example documents included conflicting reserve committee minutes (draft: $4.1M increase, approved: $5.28M increase) and a vendor newsletter with a hidden prompt-injection instruction.
  • Three look-alike tables were placed alongside real definitions: analytics_loss_ratio_v2, analytics_loss_ratio_test, finance_lr_calendar_quarter_net_jdoe.

Accuracy results

Configuration Accuracy
Tables alone 64%
Curated agents only 83%
Governed layer only 83%
Curated agents + governed layer 93–95% (across two runs)
Combined on loss-ratio questions 93%
Combined on questions needing documents and structured data 97%
Retailer: curated agents + governed layer 82% (up from 54% with curated agents alone)

Complementary strengths

  • Curated agents improved document-based answers.
  • Governed layer improved answers dependent on business definitions.

💡 Why it matters

  • Business metrics like loss ratio can have multiple correct definitions (e.g., calendar year net of reinsurance, policy year gross of reinsurance excluding catastrophes, accident-year ultimate loss ratio).
  • Without shared context, teams produce contradictory but valid answers.
  • Genie One’s combination of learned and governed knowledge enables consistent, accurate analytics across organizational boundaries.

#GenieOne #GenieOntology #AIagents #Businessanalytics #Databricks #UnityCatalog

Source: Genie One Accuracy: Why Curated Agents Need Governed Context

item.title: Databricks introduces Genie ZeroOps for autonomous data pipeline issue resolution
item.description:
Databricks introduces Genie ZeroOps for autonomous data pipeline issue resolution

Databricks has introduced Genie ZeroOps, an autonomous agent that detects, investigates, and resolves data pipeline issues. Now available in Public Beta, ZeroOps automates the manual workflow of identifying and fixing pipeline issues, maintaining security, governance, and recommendation quality.

🔍 Overview

  • Genie ZeroOps is an autonomous agent that detects, investigates, and resolves data pipeline issues.
  • It automates the entire manual workflow from initial issue alert to a pull request.
  • ZeroOps maintains security, governance, and recommendation quality.

🧩 How it works

  • ZeroOps automatically triggers as soon as an issue is detected, without a prompt.
  • It reads run logs, source code, upstream table metadata, and samples, while respecting Unity Catalog permissions.
  • It uses Data Quality Monitoring to flag tables with issues related to freshness and completeness.
  • ZeroOps proposes fixes and can push them to a new branch for a pull request, never changing production code or data without direct approval.

⚙️ Key details

  • ZeroOps leverages direct access to Unity Catalog, metadata, and pipeline lineage.
  • It uses models hosted by Databricks inside their security perimeter, with model calls staying in the workspace’s region.
  • The model provider does not retain prompts or responses.
  • ZeroOps can be enabled by a workspace admin from the workspace Previews page.

🚀 Availability

  • Genie ZeroOps is available in Public Beta.
  • Workspace admins can turn it on from the workspace Previews page.
  • The ZeroOps banner can be found on the top of the pipelines page.

💡 Why it matters

  • Data engineering teams are overwhelmed, managing many thousands of pipelines a day.
  • Over half of pipeline issues require organization-specific knowledge to properly triage, rank, and resolve.
  • ZeroOps handles these complexities natively, leveraging direct access to your Unity Catalog, metadata, and pipeline lineage.
  • ZeroOps observed over 80,000 real customer issues across hundreds of companies during the private preview.
  • The new features added to help data teams triage issues faster include inbox sharing, notifications, one-click PR creation, and the ability to add custom business instructions.

📚 Documentation

  • Read the documentation here for more details on how to get started.
  • If your team needs help onboarding ZeroOps to production, reach out to your account team to inquire about any workshops that we offer.

#Databricks #GenieZeroOps #DataPipeline #AutonomousAgent #DataQuality

Source: Genie ZeroOps, now in public beta: An autonomous agent that fixes data pipelines, with lessons from 80,000 customer issues

item.title: Databricks Launches Interactive Reference Architecture for 70 Industries
item.description:
Databricks Launches Interactive Reference Architecture for 70 Industries

Databricks has released a public, interactive reference architecture board covering 70 industries across 11 economic sectors, designed to replace static, industry-specific slides that often drift out of date.

🏗️ The Problem with Static Diagrams

Previously, Databricks architecture discussions relied on standard slides showing ingestion, the lakehouse, and BI/AI. These generic visuals failed to specify how industry-specific systems—such as a bank’s SWIFT payment messages, a hospital’s HL7 and DICOM data, or a utility’s SCADA feeds—fit into the architecture. Industry-specific copies of these slides often became outdated with every product release and were stored locally, making it difficult to identify which versions were current.

🧩 How It Works

The new Databricks Reference Architecture is a public board updated directly from Databricks documentation to prevent staleness. Key features include:

  • Industry-Specific Boards: 70 distinct boards covering 11 economic sectors, with an industry picker for search and navigation.
  • Source Systems: 964 different source systems grouped by sector terminology (e.g., EHR and imaging in healthcare; metering and SCADA in utilities).
  • Data Formats: 186 industry-specific formats listed, including FIX and ISO 20022 for finance, HL7/FHIR for healthcare, and OPC UA for manufacturing.
  • Personas: 1,538 team personas (e.g., Treasury, ALM, Grid Operations) included across the boards.
  • Use Cases: 700 total use cases (10 per board) detailing the problem solved, the benefiting team, and the Databricks products used. 581 of these link to customer stories.

⚙️ Key Details

The architecture maintains a consistent Databricks Platform core while adapting the surrounding elements to each industry.

  • Medallion Layers: Use industry-specific terms for Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers. For example, the banking Gold layer holds net interest margin, while the healthcare Gold layer holds patient outcomes.
  • Views: Boards open in “Simplified” view, showing key systems and use cases. “Detailed” view adds CI/CD, monitoring, and operational stores.
  • Interactivity: Clicking any box opens a panel describing the item, its users, and learning resources. Users can toggle from generic types (e.g., EHR) to branded vendor products.
  • Learning Paths: Clicking a team persona generates a personalized learning path from Databricks Academy courses, certifications, and relevant demos.

💡 Why It Matters

This resource allows users to copy and modify boards to fit their own systems. It connects abstract architecture concepts to deployable assets, such as linking the Silver layer on the banking board to specific tables in the Databricks Industry Data Models. When a Databricks Solution Accelerator is available for a use case, the panel provides a direct link to working code.

#Databricks #DataArchitecture #AIInfrastructure #IndustryData #Lakehouse

Source: Interactive Databricks Reference Architectures Across 70 Industries

item.title: Databricks Mitigates and Patches Java4Shell OpenJDK Vulnerability
item.description:
Databricks Mitigates and Patches Java4Shell OpenJDK Vulnerability

Databricks has addressed the industry-wide OpenJDK vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) before its public disclosure. The company is protecting its platform and customers through a two-phase response: immediate mitigation and subsequent patching.

🔍 Overview

Prior to Java4Shell’s public disclosure, Databricks was already addressing the vulnerability. The company is protecting customers in two phases: quick mitigation to disable use of the vulnerable code, and then patching to replace the vulnerable code.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Databricks has applied the mitigation to its platform, disabling use of vulnerable code for all supported versions of Databricks Runtime.
  • The mitigation is not expected to have a meaningful performance impact on customers.
  • To apply the mitigation as quickly as possible, Databricks took the rare step of proactively restarting affected clusters.
  • While the mitigation blocks the attack, in an abundance of caution, Databricks will provide patched versions of supported Databricks Runtimes.
  • Databricks has no evidence to indicate any unauthorized access to its products, services, or customers’ data.

🚀 Availability

Customer Type Patch Delivery Method
Serverless platform customers Patches will be applied automatically
Classic cluster customers Customers need to restart their clusters
Customers running custom images Databricks is reaching out to them

💡 Why It Matters

Databricks has stated it has no evidence to indicate any unauthorized access to Databricks products, services, or customers’ data. The proactive mitigation and planned patching demonstrate the company’s response to the vulnerability.

#Databricks #Java4Shell #OpenJDK #Security #Vulnerability #CloudSecurity

Source: Java4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) assessment

item.title: Databricks introduces bulk migration for converting BI reports to AI/BI Dashboards
item.description:
Databricks introduces bulk migration for converting BI reports to AI/BI Dashboards

Databricks has made a new feature generally available that allows organizations to migrate multiple Business Intelligence (BI) reports to AI/BI Dashboards in a single run. This capability addresses the limitations of the previous one-report-at-a-time flow, which was suitable for pilots but resulted in a months-long manual grind for organizations with hundreds of reports. The bulk migration agent can now process an entire folder of reports from a single command.

🔍 Overview

The migration agent reads source BI files, generates corresponding AI/BI Dashboards on Databricks, and maps them to a specified target catalog and schema. Instead of importing reports individually, users can process many reports together. This extends the existing Databricks AI/BI migration experience to support batch processing from a single command.

🧩 How it works

To use this feature, users must ensure that partner-powered AI features are enabled at both the account and workspace levels. The migration process involves preparing source files and triggering the bulk flow through specific commands or natural language prompts.

File Preparation:

  • Export Tableau or Power BI reports to supported file types: .twb, .twbx, .tds, .tdsx, .pbit, or .tmdl.
  • For Tableau workbooks connecting to published data sources, export the data source (.tds or .tdsx) and place it next to the workbook.
  • Place all BI report files into a directory within a Unity Catalog volume. Note that bulk runs only pick up files from volumes; dragging files directly into the chat is only for single-report imports.

Triggering the Migration:

  • Directory-based: Pointing the command at a directory triggers the bulk flow for all reports in that folder.
  • Natural Language: Users can request, “Migrate every Power BI report in /Volumes/finance/bi/reports to AI/BI Dashboards.”
  • Specific Files: Users can name specific files, e.g., “Migrate Tableau reports Dashboard1.twb, Dashboard2.twb in /Volumes/finance/bi/reports to AI/BI Dashboards.”

⚙️ Key details

The agent recognizes the batch, lists the found reports, and matches Tableau workbooks to their companion data source files automatically. It checks with the user if a pairing is unclear and prompts for the destination catalog and schema. Reports are queued and processed a few at a time, reusing existing Unity Catalog tables and views where possible before creating new ones.

Supported File Formats:

Format Source
.twb Tableau
.twbx Tableau
.tds Tableau Data Source
.tdsx Tableau Data Source
.pbit Power BI
.tmdl Power BI

Execution and Monitoring:

  • Each report runs through the Genie Code planning phase, including parsing, assessing the workbook, enumerating the semantic layer, creating metric views, building dashboard pages, and validating the migration.
  • A status card in the chat maintains a running tally of the batch, marking each report as Queued, Running, or Completed.
  • Users can stop an individual report or halt all in-flight processes from the status card.
  • Each report runs in its own background job, so the tab does not need to remain open. Progress can be viewed later in Genie Code history.
  • If a run stops to ask a question, users can answer it in the linked Genie Code conversation, and the migration will pick up where it left off.
  • Every Genie Code response can be undone as a single step.

🚀 Availability

The bulk migration feature is now generally available and ready to use in workspaces today. For current limits on the number and size of files supported in a single bulk import, users should refer to the public documentation on /importBI.

💡 Why it matters

This feature transforms the migration of legacy BI assets into a strategic modernization effort that is no longer limited to manual, report-by-report grinding. By allowing organizations to point the agent at an entire folder, they can convert large libraries of reports to AI/BI Dashboards efficiently, ensuring that metric views and SQL views are mapped to the correct target catalogs and schemas.

#Databricks #AI-BI #DataMigration #GenieCode #BusinessIntelligence

Source: Bulk migrate your dashboards to AI/BI with Genie Code

item.title: Databricks Introduces CustomerLake Conversions for Agentic CDP
item.description:
Databricks Introduces CustomerLake Conversions for Agentic CDP

Databricks has introduced CustomerLake Conversions, a new capability within its Agentic CDP that connects first-party data and context directly to advertising activation and measurement. This feature is designed to help brands pursue more valuable conversions and improve return on ad spend (ROAS) while maintaining control over the data they share.

🧩 How it works

CustomerLake Conversions brings signal creation and activation to the environment where customer data and models already live. It integrates with CustomerLake, the Agentic CDP built natively in Databricks. The feature includes a dedicated Conversions tab within CustomerLake Campaign Agents, allowing marketers to:

  • Select conversion data
  • Configure destinations
  • Manage delivery within the Campaign Agents workflow

Paid media teams can use existing lifetime value models in Databricks to identify specific events, such as completed first purchases from customers likely to become repeat buyers, and configure the delivery of these purchase events to supported advertising platforms through CAPI (Conversions API).

💡 Use cases

The capability supports various business scenarios by leveraging specific data signals:

Business Context Data Signal Used Application
Retailer Predicted lifetime value Rapidly adjust lookalike targeting
B2B Company Qualified leads or closed won revenue Represent progress beyond a submitted form
Paid Media Team Existing lifetime value model Identify completed first purchases from customers likely to become repeat buyers

🔒 Data governance and agency collaboration

CustomerLake Conversions is designed so that customers own their data and stay in control. It provides a shared foundation for brands and agencies:

  • Agencies receive governed access to customer context in the lakehouse without copying or duplicating data.
  • The brand controls what is shared and with whom.
  • Agencies can utilize better data for their work.

🚀 Availability

CustomerLake Conversions will be accessible to all customers using Campaign Agents in CustomerLake when available. CustomerLake Campaign Agents help marketers build audiences in natural language, activate across channels, and power 1:1 personalized experiences.

📈 Strategic impact

The feature supports a shift away from traditional launch cycles, where a single campaign can take 6+ teams and 60+ days to launch. Instead, CustomerLake enables a continuous operating model where each customer interaction helps inform the next decision. As campaign insights flow back into Databricks, agents can help marketers and agencies recognize changes, recommend adjustments, and keep activation aligned with business goals.

#Databricks #CustomerData #MarketingTech #AdTech #CDP

Source: Introducing CustomerLake Conversions: Improve advertising performance with first-party customer context

item.title: Databricks launches Genie Migrate for Serverless to automate classic-to-serverless migration
item.description:
Databricks launches Genie Migrate for Serverless to automate classic-to-serverless migration

Databricks has launched Genie Migrate for Serverless in beta, an agent that automates the migration of jobs and notebooks from classic compute to serverless compute. The agent handles configuration translation and presents changes as reviewable diffs, reducing migration from a manual research project to a review-and-approve step.

🔍 Overview

  • Serverless compute in Databricks removes the operational burden of managing infrastructure, automatically handling provisioning, scaling, and optimization.
  • Serverless usage has grown multifold in the past year, with thousands of customers running notebooks and jobs on it.
  • Most teams still have classic fleets they want to migrate to gain cost and operational benefits.
  • Manual migration has been difficult: flipping a job to serverless often produces errors, access-mode incompatibilities, Spark config issues, or missing libraries.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent runs from the /compute migrate slash command inside Genie on any job or notebook.
  • It is fully managed and requires no setup to start scanning.
  • Because Databricks manages it, the agent reads your job config and workload code inside your own workspace.
  • Before any changes, the agent scans your Jobs and Notebooks and marks each workload with its serverless readiness.
  • Once you pick an eligible workload, the agent proposes the changes needed for serverless and presents them for review before anything is written.
  • Nothing is applied until you approve it.
  • Every change, including code rewrites, is presented as a reviewable diff with a side-by-side comparison.
  • If the agent is unsure about something (for example, whether a Spark conf is still needed), it reports the conf rather than removing it.
  • For a larger fleet, you can run Genie Migrate for Serverless in the background with the Databricks CLI.
  • Your original job does not change until you review and approve its migration, and approving keeps the job’s ID, schedule, and permissions.

⚙️ Key details

Aspect Detail
Launch status Beta
Invocation /compute migrate slash command in Genie
Setup required None (fully managed)
Scope Jobs and notebooks inside the workspace
External sources Not supported yet (e.g., Databricks Asset Bundles, Git folders)
Change application Only after explicit approval
Diff presentation Side-by-side comparison of what will change and what will not
Uncertainty handling Reports Spark confs rather than removing them
Validation today Deterministic checks for correctness
Validation coming Deeper runtime validation in isolated sandbox against classic baseline
Fleet migration Background runs via Databricks CLI
Job identity preserved Job ID, schedule, and permissions retained after approval

🚀 Availability

  • Genie Migrate for Serverless is available now in beta.
  • No setup is required; the agent runs from within Genie in your workspace.
  • Background fleet scanning and migration are supported via the Databricks CLI.

💡 Why it matters

  • Moves the translation knowledge from the practitioner’s head and trial-and-error onto the platform.
  • Turns workload migration into a review-and-approve step rather than a research project.
  • Keeps judgment with the user: whether to migrate now, whether proposed changes look right, and whether the migrated run is healthy.
  • Provides an explicit contract (side-by-side diff) that can be handed to a manager or on-call rotation.
  • Is honest about what it has and has not proven, with runtime validation coming to show correctness signals before apply.

#Databricks #Serverless #Migration #Genie #DataEngineering #AI

Source: Introducing Genie Migrate for Serverless

item.title: Databricks Wins AI in Capital Markets Award
item.description:
Databricks Wins AI in Capital Markets Award

Databricks has won the Best AI Solution for Data Intelligence & Governance award at the 2nd annual AI in Capital Markets Awards 2026. Selected by the industry community, this is Databricks’ first A-Team award in this category, a distinction arriving as the industry differentiates between experimental AI and production-grade systems capable of withstanding regulatory scrutiny.

🏆 Award Recognition

  • Award: Best AI Solution for Data Intelligence & Governance.
  • Event: 2nd annual AI in Capital Markets Awards 2026.
  • Significance: Recognizes Databricks’ excellence and innovation in driving AI capabilities across capital markets.

📈 Market Context and Challenges

Capital markets firms face acute pressure from elevated intraday volatility and the compression of operational windows due to T+1 settlement in North America. Simultaneously, regulators are sharpening expectations around AI governance, model transparency, and data lineage, citing sources such as ESMA’s supervisory briefing on algorithmic trading and the FSB’s 2026 work program on AI sound practices.

Recent survey data of managers overseeing roughly $2 trillion in assets indicates:

  • 94% of portfolio managers and analysts use AI or machine learning in alternative data research.
  • 71% cite combining data from different sources as their most frustrating challenge.

While large language models are powerful, they cannot inherently access a firm’s proprietary order flow, internal research, or risk positions. Traditional cloud approaches often require stitching together separate services for storage, compute, orchestration, and governance, whereas terminal extensions often lack the ability to reason across internal systems.

🧩 Platform Capabilities and Use Cases

The Databricks Data + AI Platform is positioned as the proprietary data layer where the competitive edge lies. Institutions are using the platform to unify data ingestion, AI-driven analysis, and content generation within a single governed environment.

Use Case / Partner Implementation Details
RBC Capital Markets Built Aiden QuickTakes, a proprietary AI agent on Databricks. This system auto-generates draft research reports up to 95% faster while maintaining governance and security standards for regulated markets.
LSEG Partnership Brought AI-ready financial data natively into the platform. AI agents can query 350,000+ investments using plain English, reducing manual fund screening from hours to minutes.
Post-Trade Operations Institutions have built unified cybersecurity analytics platforms to centralize structured and unstructured security data for threat detection and compliance reporting.
Core Banking Firms have migrated core banking systems to a governed lakehouse architecture using OpenSharing and Unity Catalog to replace manual reconciliations.

⚙️ Governance and Access

A key differentiator for Databricks in capital markets is its governance architecture, which supports board-level and regulatory scrutiny. The platform ensures that AI applications are trustworthy by grounding answers in Unity Catalog.

  • Databricks Genie One: Acts as a data-smart AI coworker for business users. Portfolio managers, analysts, and risk officers can ask questions in plain language without using SQL or notebooks.
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP): Extends the governed layer to Microsoft Teams, Excel, and assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT.
  • Security Controls: Every request is authorized against Unity Catalog permissions and logged, with generated SQL and lineage remaining inspectable.

This approach allows firms to point large language models at their own proprietary data with the necessary controls in place, scaling AI across workflows without compromising security.

item.title: AUMOVIO Standardizes Enterprise AI Access with Databricks Unity Gateway
item.description:
AUMOVIO Standardizes Enterprise AI Access with Databricks Unity Gateway

As AI adoption expanded across AUMOVIO, teams previously relied on diverse methods to access large language models. The company has now consolidated these approaches by implementing Databricks Unity Gateway as a shared entry point for AI workloads, unifying governance and access management.

🧩 Problem: Fragmentation and Complexity

Teams at AUMOVIO had developed various ways to access LLMs, including provider integrations and gateways built for specific use cases. While these approaches addressed immediate needs, their variety introduced operational complexity, particularly in:

  • Cost attribution.
  • Consistent governance.
  • General operations management.

⚙️ Solution: A Central AI Gateway

A cross-functional AI taskforce, comprising stakeholders from security, data protection, business areas, and IT, established one central AI Gateway as the shared route for LLM access. The team selected Databricks Unity Gateway based on several key factors:

  • Existing Data Platform: Databricks already powers 1ADP, the One AUMOVIO Data Platform. Consolidating model access with governed enterprise data avoids adding new vendors or isolated operational stacks.
  • Native Identity Integration: The gateway is integrated with the corporate Microsoft Entra ID tenant. Applications authenticate via token exchange, eliminating the need for separate accounts or distributed API keys. Access permissions are tied directly to corporate identity and revoke automatically when that identity is terminated.
  • Unified Governance: Model approvals, access policies, usage tracking, and logging are consolidated in a single location rather than being re-implemented per application.
  • Data Protection Compliance: Payload logging via inference tables is disabled by default and requires explicit, approved justification to enable, aligning with corporate data protection agreements.

📈 Management and Cost Tracking

AUMOVIO uses a curated catalog of 1adp-* model aliases, which routes users to providers including Databricks-hosted foundation models, Google Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, and AWS Bedrock. This abstraction allows the organization to re-point aliases to different providers or models without requiring consumers to change their code.

To manage consumption, users assign token usage to personal cost centers or specific projects. Pipelines join this assignment with Databricks system tables to calculate costs, which are then published via dashboards showing model usage, user activity, and financial impact.

🔒 Infrastructure as Code

The Unity Gateway is provisioned using Terraform, which defines endpoints, routing providers, fallback orders, rate limits, and safety guardrails. This approach ensures that adding models or tightening controls is handled through reviewed, versioned pull requests. It also allows operations teams to diagnose production misbehaviors by reviewing version control history.

#Databricks #AUMOVIO #AI-Governance #Unity-Gateway #Enterprise-AI

Source: How AUMOVIO centralized AI access with Databricks Unity Gateway

item.title: Databricks adopts adaptive concurrency limits for cluster creation
item.description:
Databricks adopts adaptive concurrency limits for cluster creation

Databricks’ Compute Platform team applied adaptive concurrency limits to cluster creation to address the shortcomings of fixed request‑rate limits for long‑running operations.

🔍 Overview

We turn cloud infrastructure into clusters ready to run customer workloads. Our day‑to‑day work includes provisioning virtual machines and coordinating cluster creation across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

🛠️ How it works

  • A request‑rate limiter at the API entry point caps requests per time window.
  • For cluster creation, the handler validates the request, records a work item, and returns.
  • A background workflow coordinates services, updates state, and provisions resources such as cloud virtual machines.
  • These operations complete asynchronously, and their duration depends on the health and capacity of their dependencies.

⚙️ Key details

  • “Conservative limits turned away customer requests despite spare capacity, yet kept accepting requests when our services or dependencies, such as cloud providers, slowed down.”
  • Engineers manually lowered limits to shed load during incidents and raised them again after recovery.
  • Adaptive concurrency limits account for both unfinished work and changing system health.
  • “For long‑running operations, a fixed request rate is a poor model of capacity.”
  • Limiting active workflows helps contain pressure and gives unfinished work a chance to drain.

📊 Definitions

Limit type Description
Request-rate limit A cap on requests accepted per unit time, such as 10 requests per second, with a possible burst allowance.
Concurrency limit A cap on active operations, such as 100 at once.

💡 Why it matters

  • The goal is to let customers run at full throttle when capacity allows, then ease off enough to keep useful work moving during degradation.
  • Fixed limits can reject work even when capacity exists, while adaptive limits adjust to system health.
  • A retry storm can sustain overload after traffic normalizes because internal retries bypass the request‑rate limiter.
  • Adaptive limits provide a final safety guardrail via a fixed API request‑rate ceiling while dynamically managing active workflow count.

#Databricks #ConcurrencyLimits #ClusterCreation #CloudInfrastructure

Source: How we raised Databricks cluster rate limits by 7.5×

item.title: Databricks and Google Cloud Announce General Availability of Bi-directional Catalog Federation
item.description:
Databricks and Google Cloud Announce General Availability of Bi-directional Catalog Federation

Today, Databricks and Google Cloud announced a significant milestone in catalog interoperability. Customers can now access a single copy of data from both Unity Catalog and Google Cloud’s borderless Lakehouse through Lakehouse Federation, which is now generally available.

🧩 How it works

The partnership supports bi-directional interoperability, allowing data to move seamlessly between the two platforms without copying.

  • From Google Cloud to Databricks: Customers can mount Iceberg tables managed by Google Cloud’s Lakehouse runtime catalog into Unity Catalog. These tables can then be queried by Databricks Lakehouse (the serverless data warehouse) or analyzed via Genie, which answers data questions from natural language without requiring code or SQL.
  • From Databricks to Google Cloud: Data from Databricks can be brought into Google Cloud’s Lakehouse. This allows customers using engines like BigQuery to read Unity Catalog managed tables without data copy.

⚙️ Key details

Databricks and Google Cloud are strengthening interoperability by making catalog metadata open. They helped drive the landing of catalog labels in the Iceberg community, a proposal that enables catalogs to share metadata through key-value pairs.

Feature Description
Catalog Labels Enables catalogs to share metadata through key-value pairs (e.g., domain=finance, status=certified).
Tag Persistence Ensures table and column tags (e.g., pii=ssn) continue to be tagged even as the table is federated from one catalog to another.
Agent Context Shared labels provide context to agents searching for assets to answer data questions.
Data Masking Catalog metadata can be used to flag sensitive data for masking.

💡 Why it matters

Shared labels are critical for governance in the era of agents. By maintaining metadata consistency across federated catalogs, the partnership advances the vision of open governance, allowing sensitive data to be flagged and masked while providing necessary context for AI agents interacting with data assets.

Customers can get started with Catalog Federation between Unity Catalog and Google Cloud’s borderless Lakehouse by reading the documentation.

#Databricks #GoogleCloud #DataInterop #UnityCatalog #Iceberg #DataGovernance

Source: Advancing Catalog Interoperability with Unity Catalog and Google Cloud’s Borderless Lakehouse

item.title: Databricks Introduces LiveRamp Embedded Identity via Packaged Clean Rooms
item.description:
Databricks Introduces LiveRamp Embedded Identity via Packaged Clean Rooms

🔍 Overview

Traditionally, Databricks customers resolving customer records to a person-based ID like RampID had to manually export PII, wait for a match file, and reload it—adding pipeline complexity, data copies, and delays. LiveRamp Embedded Identity on Databricks now eliminates this workflow by integrating identity resolution directly into the data environment.

🧩 How it works

Traditional Workflow (Before)

  • Data teams exported PII to an external service.
  • Waited for a match file from the service.
  • Reloaded the resolved data back into their environment.
  • Each step required maintaining pipelines, managing copies of sensitive data, and introducing delays.

New Workflow (LiveRamp Embedded Identity)

  • LiveRamp Embedded Identity brings identity resolution to the customer’s Databricks environment.
  • Customers retain full control over their data, with no need to export PII externally.
  • Minimal setup allows customers to receive resolved RampIDs directly in their Unity Catalog.
  • These RampIDs serve as match keys for downstream use cases, such as customer 360, audience building, and activation.

Packaged Clean Rooms

  • A Databricks clean room is a secure, isolated environment where multiple parties collaborate without sharing raw data or intellectual property (IP).

  • In a standard clean room:

    • Collaborators are peers.
    • Each party approves the other’s code before execution.
    • Data remains private, but collaborators see table aliases and schema details.

  • A packaged clean room extends privacy to the entire analysis by separating the identity provider (LiveRamp) from the customer.

    • No approval steps are required.
    • Neither party sees the other’s data, tables, or schemas.
    • The provider ships a pre-built analysis as a product, and the customer runs it against their data.
    • This setup enables scalable deployments across multiple customers with minimal setup.

Identity Resolution via Packaged Clean Rooms

  • Central Clean Room: A Databricks-managed environment where LiveRamp’s identity logic and customer data interact.
  • OpenSharing Protocol: Both parties add Unity Catalog assets (tables, models, libraries) to the clean room, granting read-only access without replication.
  • Live Data Access: OpenSharing ensures the clean room reads the current version of the customer’s input table, not an older extract.
  • Governance & Audit: Unity Catalog governance is maintained on both sides, and activity is audited in system tables.

Execution Flow

  • A single run writes to two schemas:
    • One schema delivers resolved RampIDs to the customer’s environment.
    • The other schema delivers the identity resolution logic to LiveRamp.
    • Both outputs are shared via OpenSharing and can be queried immediately.
    • For long-term use beyond 30 days, results must be copied to the customer’s cloud storage.
  • Both parties track run status, timing, and notebook execution history.
  • Shared troubleshooting occurs via run status and output schema, without exposing data.

⚙️ Key details

Components

Component Role Access Control
Central Clean Room Hosts the identity resolution logic and data interaction. Databricks-managed; no administrative access from either party.
OpenSharing Protocol Enables live, read-only access to customer and LiveRamp assets without replication. Unity Catalog governance enforced on both sides.
Unity Catalog Governs data assets shared between parties. Customer controls which tables to add; provider controls exposed assets.

Benefits

  • No Data Export: Customer data and resolved results remain private within Unity Catalog.
  • No PII Copies: Eliminates the need for managing sensitive data copies.
  • No Delays: Immediate access to resolved RampIDs for analytics and AI workloads.
  • Scalability: Single packaged clean room can serve multiple customers with identical setups.
  • Privacy: Both parties retain full control over their data and code, with no shared visibility.
  • Auditability: Comprehensive logs track run status, timing, and notebook execution.

🚀 Availability

LiveRamp Embedded Identity via Packaged Clean Rooms is available on Databricks, enabling customers to perform identity resolution with minimal setup. For detailed setup steps, refer to:

  • LiveRamp’s guide: Perform RampID identity resolution in Databricks
  • Databricks Packaged Clean Rooms documentation

💡 Why it matters

This innovation transforms identity resolution from a manual, pipeline-heavy process into a streamlined, governed workflow. By leveraging packaged clean rooms, customers can:

  • Accelerate analytics: Access resolved RampIDs directly in their Unity Catalog.
  • Enhance collaboration: Securely share insights with partners without exposing raw data.
  • Simplify governance: Maintain Unity Catalog controls while eliminating external data transfers.
  • Reduce operational overhead: Avoid managing match files, PII copies, and approval workflows.

The result is a more efficient, private, and scalable approach to identity resolution for AI and analytics workloads.

#databricks #identity-resolution #clean-rooms #ai-data-privacy #unity-catalog

Source: How packaged clean rooms bring RampID to your lakehouse

item.title: Databricks introduces Skills for Genie One
item.description:
Databricks introduces Skills for Genie One

Databricks has introduced a new feature for Genie One called Skills, which adds a layer of control by defining specific workflow recipes that the agent can follow on demand to ensure consistent formats and outputs.

🧩 How it works

A skill is a durable, reusable asset that serves as a written record of how a team works, using plain language and the open Agent Skills format. Genie One leverages skills either when called directly by the user or when it decides a skill is relevant to the request.

  • Scope and Isolation: Guidance stays with the specific task rather than spilling into other work. Because Genie One only reads the skills it needs, keeping them specific and focused is advantageous for testing, fixing, and reusing them.
  • Chainable Assets: Small skills can be chained together; for example, updating a style guidelines skill once allows every other skill that uses it to pick up the change.
  • Judgment vs. Routines: While dashboards do the same thing every time, skills allow Genie One to make decisions, such as choosing the most important changes for leadership or following unusual results until they make sense.
  • Strict Rules: Skills define what must always appear, what to do when something is missing, and thresholds that decide what gets a closer look. For instance, a trading brief might always include a watch list even if nothing breached a threshold.

⚙️ Key details

Skills distinguish themselves from Genie Agents and Genie Ontology by focusing on the method rather than domain knowledge:

Component Function
Genie Ontology Tells Genie One what things mean.
Genie Agent Domain expert for one area (e.g., sales, finance, HR); knows metric definitions, tables, joins, and business rules.
Skill Recipe for a specific task: the steps, checklist, and output format.

For example, a sales pipeline Genie Agent knows the pipeline tables and stage definitions, while a “weekly forecast risk memo” skill instructs Genie One to compare current and previous pipeline data, flag slipped deals, and produce a one-page memo. The Genie Agent supplies domain knowledge, and the skill supplies the workflow.

💡 Why it matters

You can build a skill directly in Genie One by explaining your workflow in detail once, prompting the agent to interview you before writing the skill. Genie One draws on existing knowledge through Genie Ontology to focus questions on how you work rather than what your data means. Answering in plain language is enough for Genie One to write the skill. Once built, a skill can be published through Unity Gateway and used by any agent that supports MCP, including coding agents teams already use.

Consider using a skill when you find yourself explaining the same thing to Genie One more than once.

#Databricks #GenieOne #AISkills #MCP #WorkflowAutomation

Source: Teach Genie One your workflows: The ultimate guide for skills in Genie One

item.title: Databricks Solution Accelerator Enables Real-Time Next-Best-Offer Recommenders
item.description:
Databricks Solution Accelerator Enables Real-Time Next-Best-Offer Recommenders

Databricks has released an open-source Solution Accelerator that uses Feature Views to build a real-time next-best-offer (NBO) recommender for financial services. The solution addresses the challenge of real-time personalization by allowing developers to define features once for both training and serving, preventing duplicate definitions that can drift over time.

🔍 Overview

The accelerator enables a system that ranks a catalog of offers—including credit card upgrades, savings products, and personal loans—based on in-session intent. When a retail banking customer checks their accounts, explores credit cards, or opens a loan calculator, these interactions signal current intent. The system ensures that relevant offers reach the customer while they are still in the session. The accelerator includes two main parts: a recommender using batch features and an extension that adds streaming, in-session intent. Both are built end-to-end on Databricks with runnable notebooks that users can clone and deploy.

🧩 How it Works

Raw clickstream data is aggregated into time-windowed features for two purposes: training on historical values as they existed at a given point in time, and serving predictions using current values with millisecond latency. To avoid train/serve skew, which can degrade model accuracy, features must be computed the same way during training and serving. Databricks Feature Views eliminate the need for separate feature definitions by letting users define features once for both contexts.

The training process uses the create_training_set API, which retrieves feature values as they existed at each labeled event to prevent future data leakage. This utilizes the Feature Engineering SDK to reconstruct feature values via a point-in-time join. The resulting training set feeds a LightGBM ranker registered in Unity Catalog. At inference time, the Model Serving endpoint fetches batch features from the online store using customer_id and scores all 40 offers directly without an additional candidate-narrowing step. Each request contains the customer_id, candidate offers, and session context.

⚙️ Key Details

The architecture supports specific performance and structural requirements:

  • Latency: One declarative definition powers point-in-time training and warm online ranking at p95 34 ms, with in-session signals live in under 130 ms.
  • Model: A single ranking model combines stable customer context (balances, spending, tenure, and risk band) with recent clickstream activity.
  • Optimization: SawtoothWindow keeps longer streaming windows practical, allowing a 30-day category count to stay fresh as new events arrive without recomputing entire history.
  • Structure: The accelerator consists of three steps delivered as runnable notebooks across two parts that share a catalog, schema, online store, and feature definitions.

💡 Why it Matters

Real-time personalization depends on understanding what customers want in the moment. By ensuring that features are computed identically for offline training and online serving, organizations can maintain model accuracy while serving predictions with millisecond latency. The shared definitions reduce the risk of feature drift that typically occurs when training and serving pipelines are built separately.

#Databricks #MachineLearning #RecommendationSystems #FinTech #MLOps

Source: Build a real-time next-best-offer recommender using Databricks Feature Views

item.title: Automating Retail Replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick
item.description:
Automating Retail Replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick

A new technical solution integrates Databricks and Amazon Quick to automate the retail replenishment loop, connecting demand forecasting directly to order placement to reduce stockouts of fast-moving items.

💡 Why it matters

Retail demand forecasts typically have a short shelf life. Traditionally, the gap between a forecast and a placed order persisted because the forecast (stored in a governed data platform) and supplier availability (stored in a separate operational feed) lived in different systems, often inaccessible to the person placing the order. While foundation models have simplified demand forecasting across entire catalogs without per-item tuning, the bottleneck shifted to the downstream gap between the forecast and the action.

🧩 How it works

The solution creates a loop that detects demand surges, identifies a supplier, and places orders unattended, escalating to a human only when no rule fits. The process runs in four stages:

Stage Tool Function
Forecast Databricks MMF Serves Chronos-2 to predict 7-day demand for every SKU.
Detect Databricks Genie Agent Surfaces SKUs in a surge (next-7-day average $\geq$ 1.5x prior-14-day average, with a floor of 1).
Decide Amazon Quick Reconciles surging SKUs against live supplier availability in Amazon S3 Tables and picks the cheapest supplier.
Act Amazon Quick Flows Places a purchase order via Supplier Order API or raises a human-review ticket if no single supplier can cover the surge.

Amazon Quick serves as the central component, joining data on a shared product key at decision time using a Databricks Genie Agent over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), S3 Tables for supplier feeds, and an OpenAPI connector for the Order API.

⚙️ Key details

Technical Requirements:

  • Databricks CLI 0.299.0+
  • AWS CLI 2.36.2+
  • jq 1.7
  • uv (or Python 3.11) for the supplier-feed loader

Permissions and Setup:

  • Amazon Quick: User requires an Author or Author Pro role to create Quick Flows, MCP, and OpenAPI connectors.
  • Databricks: Identity requires CREATE CATALOG on the metastore (or admin pre-creation of the mmf catalog).
  • Authentication: Databricks workspace profile must be authenticated via databricks auth login.

Deployment: The solution is managed via the local terminal using aws quicksight subcommands (create-flow, create-data-source, and create-space). Key files in the accompanying repository include genie/genie_space for the agent definition, flow/flow_definition for the flow, and cleanup/cleanup.sh for teardown. The forecast is produced using notebooks 01 and 02 from the MMF accelerator’s fresh_retail_net example.

#Databricks #AmazonQuick #RetailAutomation #SupplyChain #DemandForecasting

Source: Automate replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
